disclaimer.body: MirrorPilot is a free community project. It does not run mirrors of its own and it does not proxy image traffic. It measures sources that others operate, and helps you copy images into a registry you control.
disclaimer.no_warranty: Provided as is, with no warranty. See the licence for details.
disclaimer.official_only: Third-party mirrors are convenient, not authoritative. Check a digest against the official registry when it matters.
disclaimer.title: Before you rely on this

probe.egress_body: These measurements are taken from this panel's own network egress — the machine or container it runs in. That is the path a docker pull on this host would take, and it says nothing about any other network.
probe.egress_direct: No proxy variables are set, so the probe connects directly. A pull from another machine, another city or another provider can rank these mirrors very differently.
probe.egress_proxied: This process has a proxy configured, so the probe goes through it. What gets measured is the proxy's path to each mirror as much as the mirror itself.
probe.error.target: The image to measure is not usable. Check the repository and reference in Settings.
probe.error.unavailable: This build has no probe engine wired up, so mirrors cannot be measured here.
probe.limits_body: What these numbers do and do not tell you:
probe.limits_cache: A tag can be answered from a mirror's own cache. Two mirrors measured in the same batch may not have served identical bytes — the resolved digest column is what tells you.
probe.limits_daemon_json: A mirror in registry-mirrors only ever covers Docker Hub. It does nothing for ghcr.io, quay.io, gcr.io or mcr.microsoft.com, which people routinely assume otherwise about.
probe.limits_egress: The vantage point is this host only. A mirror that wins here can lose from somewhere else.
probe.limits_rate_limit: Rate limiting is reported as its own result rather than as a failure. A 429 says the mirror would not talk to us right now; it does not say the mirror is broken.
probe.results_note: One row per mirror, newest measurement each. A dash means the step produced no number — either it never ran, or it finished faster than this host's clock could resolve. That is not the same as zero.
probe.run_all_hint: Runs one after another with a few in flight. A few seconds per mirror; a slow or unreachable one takes up to fifteen seconds.
probe.subtitle: Measure how each mirror actually performs from this machine.
probe.target_note: Every mirror is asked for the same image. A digest is a better choice than a tag: a tag can be answered from a stale cache, which makes the comparison quietly unfair.
probe.title: Speed test
settings.probe_hint: Every mirror is asked for this image. Leave a field blank to use the default shown in grey.
settings.probe_reference_hint: A digest, if you have one, makes runs comparable: a tag may be answered from a mirror's cache and be a different image on two mirrors.
settings.subtitle: Language, appearance, and the image mirrors are measured against.
settings.title: Settings
setup.explainer: The password has two jobs. It logs you in, and it derives the key that encrypts the GitHub and registry credentials you store later. Neither is written to disk.
setup.password_hint: At least %d characters. It also encrypts the credentials you save here, so if you lose it they cannot be recovered.
setup.subtitle: Choose the password that protects this panel.
setup.title: Set up MirrorPilot
sources.col.name: Name
sources.delete_confirm: Delete this mirror? Its measurement history goes with it.
sources.enabled_hint: "In use" decides what a batch run covers. Measuring one mirror by hand always works, whether or not it is switched on.
sources.error.builtin_readonly: That mirror ships with the binary. You can turn it off, but not edit or delete it — otherwise the trust badge next to it would mean nothing.
sources.error.duplicate_id: That identifier is already taken. Pick another.
sources.field.enabled: Use this mirror in batch runs
sources.field.id_hint: Lowercase letters, digits and dashes. It is the key everything else is stored under, so it cannot change later.
sources.field.insecure: This mirror is only reachable over plain HTTP
sources.field.insecure_hint: Plain HTTP cannot detect tampering. Such mirrors are listed so they can be measured, and are never a good default.
sources.field.name: Name
sources.field.provider_hint: Who runs it. A fact about them, not a rating of the mirror.
sources.field.scope_hint: A mirror only helps for the registries it actually mirrors. One that proxies ghcr.io does nothing for a Docker Hub pull.
sources.field.trust_hint: How much is published about the operator — not how fast or how reliable the mirror is.
sources.field.url_hint: The registry endpoint, with no path. This is the value that would go in registry-mirrors.
sources.id_immutable: The identifier cannot change: your settings and this mirror's measurement history are keyed on it.
sources.subtitle: The mirrors this panel measures, including any you add yourself.
sources.title: Mirrors
sources.trust_body: The trust grade records how much is publicly known about whoever runs a mirror. It is a statement about transparency — not a security guarantee, and not a speed rating.
sources.trust_no_guarantee: Third-party mirrors are convenient, not authoritative. Check a digest against the official registry when it matters.
unlock.banner: Locked: your stored credentials are unreadable, so scheduled syncing is paused. Unlock to resume it. You will only be asked once per restart.
unlock.subtitle: MirrorPilot restarted and its encryption key is no longer in memory.
unlock.title: Unlock
